business_problem: FLORA needed to provide professional creative teams with fast, reliable AI workflows for text, image, and video while protecting clients' proprietary branding and unreleased assets. Third-party model aggregators struggled with peak traffic, and the team required real-time image prototyping, flexible capacity, and enterprise data controls.
solution_summary: FLORA moved its AI workloads from third-party model aggregators directly to Google after aggregators struggled with peak traffic, latency, and reliability. Its node-based creative canvas brings text, image, and video work into one professional workflow, and an intent-based router selects the model for each task. Agents built with Gemini 3.7 Flash balance output quality, cost, and latency; Gemini models power most workflows, with Nano Banana supporting image generation and 4K upscaling, Gemini Omni supporting video generation and editing, and Flash Lite also used in creative workflows. Google Cloud enterprise data controls address privacy and compliance requirements for proprietary client assets. The story names BigQuery as a Google Data Cloud service, but its role and the platform's ingestion, storage, or external interfaces are not described, so no data pipeline is inferred. Direct access to Google reduced latency and operating costs.
